posts.text:
Weekend thoughts…

Bitcoin stops losses have been triggered and exchanges likely have rinsed clients, and gone long (along with the crypto whale insiders)

Gold and silver peaked in anticipation of rate high cycle and an inflation fighting Fed.  

Since then commodities have been successfully smashed, housing market has gotten very week.  

Concerns of a slowdown in Ai data centers build out has in part lead to a massive sell off in uranium equities despite strong uranium spot and long term contract prices.  Nuclear power new builds, restarts and life extensions are real and the supply demand balance long term is extremely positive for uranium price.  

With major banks and brokers having dropped hard 20-30% etc.  the Fed is likely well aware of the balance sheet risk that can quickly develop and lead to a 2008 like collapse.  

I expect with this weeks sell off we don’t need much more selling, but only time to pass for it to be clear that unemployment is a concern and consumer spending along with housing starts is collapsing. 

Talk will shift to holding rates at this level and then quickly the narrative will change to the need to cut and the Fed being behind the curve. 

The oil price move is entirely due to war and it’s a major deterrent for economic activity. Here in the Caribbean  tourism has really dropped off a there’s barely any yachts cruising around these days.  Barely anyone going out fishing either.  $8.25 a gallon seems to have crushed demand significantly. 

I think the dramatic sell off in silver is enough to get people bottom fishing in size.  

Gold and silver will turn and rally well in advance of the narrative change from rate hike to rate cuts.  

There’s also been a lot of commentary on risk off,  plenty of I told you so’s and dunking on commodity and tech bulls.   I love to see this along with the overall bearish talk and fear indicators.  

Technically we oversold in many measures… so all said, I’m feeling extremely bullish for a strong recovery in most smashed commodity stocks and especially favouring uranium and silver. 

It was only a couple months ago we had people screaming about ‘you can’t own enough copper’.  Now there’s concern that ‘Dr Copper’ is pointing to a sick economy and a looming recession.  

With many trillions in market cap evaporating you can bet that consumer spending is gonna take a hit.  The stats that will come out soon will confirm the economy slow down and the likelihood of rate cuts being called for.
